messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired: PD-PROD-1891 — rate-limiter error-rate threshold breached; automated page to on-call

pagerduty: Paging alice (oncall) — triggered by service: rate-limiter-prod (high 5xx rate)

alice (oncall): ack — i'm on it, joining the channel now :eyes:

bob (sre): saw the pager, pulling graphs. Grafana link: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/rate-limiter/rl-overview?panelId=3 — 502s spike from limiter started ~3m ago

alice (oncall): quick question — is this global or limited to a region? customers reporting 429s and 502s

carla (infra): checking k8s — rate-limiter pods are flapping, CrashLoopBackOff on one; others overloaded. `kubectl get pods -n prod | grep rate-limiter` shows 3/5 ready

dave (platform): recent deploy? deploy-bot shows a config push ~10m ago: `deploy-bot: config:rate-limiter:global_quota_override=100` — that was rolled out across all clusters

bob (sre): suspect misapplied global quota. The override might have been intended for a canary but went to all. that's why all tenants hit stricter limits -> cascading failures on our internal backpressure

alice (oncall): OK mitigation plan: 1) remove the global_quota_override (rollback config) 2) scale limiter replicas to absorb backlog 3) add temporary allowlist for critical customers

dave (platform): i can revert the config immediately. rolling back config change to previous commit now.

deploy-bot: Starting rollback: config-service @ 1778034558 -> deploying rollback id: cfg-rollback-317

carla (infra): scaling up rate-limiter: `kubectl scale deploy rate-limiter -n prod --replicas=6` — scaling started

eva (support-bizops): ps — which customers are impacted? support queue showing multiple enterprise tenants complaining about 429s, highest priority: acme-inc and fintool. I'll draft a status note once we know ETA

bob (sre): attaching recent logs snippet:
```
2026-03-14T12:14:01Z rate-limiter[pid=23]: applied global_quota_override=100
2026-03-14T12:15:12Z rate-limiter[pid=23]: E[limiter] drop request tenant=acme-inc reason=quota_exceeded
2026-03-14T12:16:34Z rate-limiter[pid=23]: E[http] upstream 502 on req id=abc123
```

carla (infra): rollback finished — config reverted. rolling pods to pick up change (`kubectl rollout restart deploy/rate-limiter -n prod`)

alice (oncall): are error rates coming down?

bob (sre): partial improvement. 502s dropped ~60% in the last 90s but some tenants still see 429s due to backlog and token bucket state.

dave (platform): adding emergency bypass for enterprise tenants: pushing an allowlist to rate-limiter to exempt acme-inc and fintool until state drains

deploy-bot: Allowlist change deployed: allowlist:add [acme-inc,fintool] by dave — change id allow-2026-317

alice (oncall): good. that's buying time. set pager to quiet for this incident? it's still P1 until customer impact resolved.

pagerduty: Incident PD-PROD-1891 acknowledged by alice (oncall) at 2026-03-14T12:18:20Z

eva (support-bizops): posting interim status to customers: "We're seeing rate limiting regressions caused by a config change that was rolled back; we've applied an emergency allowlist for impacted enterprise customers while we complete recovery. We'll provide an update in 15 minutes." — posting now to status.redwood.com/incidents/PD-1891

bob (sre): backlog drain estimate ~8-12m depending on traffic. monitoring token-bucket refill and retry queues.

carla (infra): one pod still in CrashLoopBackOff — investigating underlying OOMs, may be memory leak triggered by new config. isolating node and collecting core dump

alice (oncall): target: stabilize customer-facing errors to <1% within 15m. if not, escalate to full SRE all-hands and exec notif.

dave (platform): i'm going to run a quick healthcheck script to ensure other services not impacted: `./tools/healthcheck --service rate-limiter --full`

bob (sre): logs show repeated redis connection timeouts immediately after override; might be secondary - the sudden drop in throughput causes bursts/backpressure into cache layer

alice (oncall): handoff plan — i'll stay with incident for 20 more minutes, then hand to bob for ongoing remediation and postmortem. bob, you're on followup if we hit the 15m window

bob (sre): ack, will take over. I'll open the incident ticket and collect runbook items. starting incident ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-2026-1891

eva (support-bizops): logged the customer-impact brief in the ticket and updated support playbook. customers notified.

carla (infra): pod that was OOMing recovered after restart, replicas stable at 6/6 ready now. no further CrashLoopBackOffs.

bob (sre): metrics look stable; 429s down to baseline for most tenants, acme-inc still seeing retries but traffic declining. marking incident as mitigated — keeping PD incident open for postmortem

alice (oncall): formally closing pager escalation to paging channel but leaving incident thread here for handoff notes. thanks everyone for quick responses :thumbsup:

pagerduty: Incident PD-PROD-1891 status changed to "Mitigated" by bob (sre) at 2026-03-14T12:40:20Z

bob (sre): followups: 1) postmortem draft (owner: bob) 2) tighten CI checks to prevent global flag rollouts without canary 3) add an emergency override endpoint protected by MFA 4) alert tweak: split quota-exceed from downstream 502s to avoid noisy paging

dave (platform): I'll open PRs for config gating and emergency endpoint design.

eva (support-bizops): i'll coordinate customer follow-ups and SLA credits if needed.

alice (oncall): handoff to bob complete. bob you own the incident ticket for postmortem + sev report. handing off now.

bob (sre): taking ownership, noted. moving followup items to postmortems and eng-releases to track config release changes.

alice (oncall): thanks team — ending active duty on this one.

(incident thread archived for post-incident analysis)
